title: Unreadable apply claim wedges the whole outbox
evidence: packages/kernel/src/decision/apply.ts:117-127 (pre-fix) built the claim with readPacket/currentDecisions/outcomeOf, each `must`-throwing; lib/decision/v1/applier.ts:75-86 turns the throw into a logged error each drain
body:
## Summary
takeApply threw on a claim whose stored rows the door refused, rolling the claim back so the row headed the due order forever.

## Description
Fixed: an AppError from the claim's reads now moves the row to stuck with the door's sentence (fail-loud-classification-default).

## Flow
- corrupt one committed packet body
- drainApplies

## Expected impact
Every other packet's apply is delivered; the bad one shows stuck and is redriven after repair.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one bad row no longer blocks the outbox
Before: drainApplies throws; 0 of 1 healthy applies delivered
After: healthy applied, poisoned stuck attempts 1 with reason, 1 apply-stuck event
Method: gate - packages/kernel/test/decision.apply.test.ts red then green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: gatePacketFact scanned every packet per gate read
body:

## Summary

## Description

- lib latestAttempt/ratifies delegate

After: 1 implementation (predicted)

title: readPacketView re-reads head and decision rows several times
instrument: the counting reader in packages/kernel/test/decision.view.test.ts around readPacketView for a cull and a blind pair
evidence: packages/kernel/src/decision/view.ts:34-73 calls head, readPacket (head), rows, currentDecisions (head+rows), revealPicks (head+rows+items+picks), items, returnedPlan, applyStatus
body:
## Summary
One packet view issues ~7 statements for a cull and ~14 for a blind pair, with rows() read up to 3 times.

## Description
Derive current decisions and outcomes from the one rows() read (currentOf + toDecision) and pass head along; keep revealPicks' SQL guard as the only path to a pick.

## Flow
- count statements per readPacketView
- fold the duplicate reads
- recount

## Expected impact
Fewer statements per Board sheet render; low absolute cost.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - statements per packet view
Before: ~7 cull / ~14 blind (walked, not counted)
After: ~4 / ~7 predicted
Method: simulation - counted by reading, not instrumented this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: A blind pair stays revealed after the operator undoes its verdict
evidence: packages/kernel/src/decision/read.ts:48-58 judgedRows and :141-147 revealPicks count ANY operator row with a verdict, undone rows included; planUndo (core.ts:125) appends the inverse so the old row persists
body:
## Summary
Patch a pair, see the machine pick and grades, undo, re-judge: the re-judgement is made sighted and still counts as a blind agreement.

## Description
read.ts reveals on 'ever judged', not 'currently judged'. Re-hiding cannot unsee; the honest options are to keep revealing but mark the pair's later verdict as sighted (decision-records: proving what the decider saw), or exclude such pairs from agreement. Which is a product call about the measurement.

## Flow
- pick a on pair s1
- revealPicks shows machine pick
- undo
- pick b
- agrees computed as if blind

## Expected impact
Machine-vs-operator agreement can be biased by sighted re-judgements.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - blind measurement integrity
Before: sighted re-judgements counted as blind
After: depends on the chosen rule
Method: simulation - the rule is a direction, not a figure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
